Part A: Basic Operations
A1 Create v as the sequence 5, 10, 15,..., 50 using seq(). Print its length, sum and mean.
```{r}
v <- seq(5, 50, by = 5)

length(v)
sum(v)
mean(v)
```

A2 Create that repeats the vector c(1,2,3) four times, and z that repeats each elements of c(1,2,3) four times. Print both.
```{r}
w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)

print(w)
print(z)
```


A3 Compute and print: the remainder of 17 divided by 5, the integer division of 17 by 5, 2 to the power of 10, the square root of 144, and pi rounded to 3 decimals.
```{r}
a = 17
b = 5
a %% b     
a %/%      
2^10        
sqrt(144)    
round(pi, 3) 
```

A4 Given a<- c(2, 4, 6, 8) and b <-(1, 3, 5, 7), print a + b, a * b, the logical comparison a > b, and the dot product sum(a * b).
```{r}
a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)

a + b
a * b
a > b
sum(a * b)
```

A5 Use paste() to produce "Student-1" "Student-2" "Student-3". Then identify the datatype of 42, 42L, "42", 41i, and TRUE. What are its output?
```{r}
paste0("Students", 1:3, sep = "-")

typeof(42)
typeof(42L)
typeof("42")
typeof(42L)
typeof(42L)
```

Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements

B1 Create a data frame students with 8 rows and these coloumns (use stringsAsFactors = FALSE; sex is "M" or "F"):
```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

students

```

B2 Display the structure, dimensions, coloumns names, and summary of students.
```{r}
str(students)

dim(students)

names(students)

summary(students)
```

B3 Add a coloumn average = the mean of midterm and final for each students, rounded to 1 decimal.
```{r}
students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)

print(students)
```

B4 Add a logical coloumn passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 and attendance >= 75.
```{r}
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75

print(students)
```

B5 Using ifelse(), add coloumn standing with these values based on average:
```{r}
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                     ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good",
                            "Needs Support"))
students
```


B6 Write a function classify(score) that uses an if / else if / else chain and returns "Distinction" for 85 or above, "Merit" for 70 to 84, "Pass" for 50 to 69, and "Fail" below 50. Test it with sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify) and print the result.
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}
```


Part C: rbind() and cbind()

C1 Create a data frame new_students with two students. Its columns must match the original, including average, passed and standing, computed the same way:

• id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92
• id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80

Use rbind() to append them to students, saving the result as students_all.
```{r}

new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students

```


C2 Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6). Use cbind() to attach it to students_all as a column named quiz. Confirm the result is still a data frame with class().
```{r}

quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)

students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)

print(students_all)
print(class(students_all))

```


C3 Create the matrix m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final) and use rbind() to append a final row containing the column means, labelled "mean".
```{r}

m <- cbind(
  midterm = students_all$midterm,
  final = students_all$final
)

print(m)

m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))

print(m)

```


C4 In a comment (2-3 sentences), explain what error rbind() produces if the data frames have different column names, and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatch()


tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL }).
```{r}

bad <- students[1, ]

names(bad)[1] <- "student_id"

result <- tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    return(NULL)
  }
)

print(result)

```
# rbind() gives an error when the column names are different.
# tryCatch() is used to catch the error and show the message instead of stopping the program.

Part D: Subsetting

Use students_all (with quiz) for all questions. Print every result.
D1 Extract the name column in three ways: $, [["name"]], and [ , "name"].
```{r}

print(students_all$name)

print(students_all[["name"]])

print(students_all[, "name"])

```


D2 Extract rows 2 to 5 and only the columns name, midterm, final.
```{r}

print(students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")])

```


D3 Using logical subsetting, select students withattendance' above 90.
```{r}

print(students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ])

```


D4 Using subset(), select students of sex "F" in section "A" or "C" whose final is at least 75; return only name, section and final.
```{r}

result <- subset(students_all,
                 sex == "F" &
                 section %in% c("A", "C") &
                 final >= 75,
                 select = c(name, section, final))

print(result)

```


D5 Use which.max() and which.min() to report the name of the student with the highest and lowest average.
```{r}

highest <- which.max(students_all$average)
lowest <- which.min(students_all$average)

print(students_all$name[highest])
print(students_all$name[lowest])

```


D6 Sort students_all by average in descending order, then print the top 3 rows.
```{r}

sorted_students <- students_all[order(students_all$average, decreasing = TRUE), ]

print(head(sorted_students, 3))

```

Part E: Basic Factors

E1 Convert section and sex in students_all to factors with factor(). Print levels() of each.
```{r}

students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)

print(levels(students_all$section))
print(levels(students_all$sex))

```

E2 Use table() to count students per sex and per section.
*Try the two-way table of sex by section. table(students_all$sex, students_all$section). What is the output?
```{r}

print(table(students_all$sex))

print(table(students_all$section))

print(table(students_all$sex, students_all$section))

```
The table shows how many female and male students are in each section. It helps me see the number of students based on their sex and section.

E3 Print as.integer() of the sex factor. In a comment, explain what the integers represent.
```{r}

print(as.integer(students_all$sex))

```
# The numbers represent the codes assigned to each sex.
# 1 means F and 2 means M.

E4 Create a new factor sex_label from sex using factor() with levels = c ("F", "M") and labels = c("Female", "Male"). Add it to students_all and print its levels(),
```{r}

students_all$sex_label <- factor(
  students_all$sex,
  levels = c("F", "M"),
  labels = c("Female", "Male")
)

print(students_all)
print(levels(students_all$sex_label))

```


E5 Print summary() of sex_label. Then using logical subsetting and mean(), print the mean average for each level of sex_label.
```{r}

print(summary(students_all$sex_label))

female_average <- mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Female"])

male_average <- mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Male"])

print(female_average)
print(male_average)

```
